name: security
description: The security architecture: controls, threats and trust boundaries in S1–S5 across every layer of a design, on NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 and CSF 2.0
agent_guide: Layer S is the security architecture, beside the design's layers. It holds security controls (SEC.S.SecurityControl: an NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control, with its control_id, CSF 2.0 function and implementation_status), threats (SEC.S.Threat: STRIDE category, likelihood, impact) and trust boundaries, each in one security layer: S1 business, S2 service domains (BIAN), S3 data, S4 application, S5 technology — the security view of the design layer of that name. Its links into the design: PROTECTS (a control protects a record), ENFORCED_BY (what carries the control out), THREATENS (a threat applies to a record), BOUNDS (a trust boundary round a zone or component); inside S, mitigates (control to threat). Every record in a report carries design_layer — its layer as this design names and numbers it (e.g. A5 Technology): quote that, never the report's own 'layer' or the number in a type name, which are in the numbering security's rules are written in. Reports: review — the security standard's rule results (cite the rule id, e.g. SEC-S08, and the record), the records no control protects, any S-layer left empty; coverage — which records are protected and by what: a control of its own (PROTECTS) or, for a field, through its data entity (protected_through); threats — the STRIDE checklist: prompts for a person, never threats the design holds; document — the full security review (sections 1 findings, 2 records no control protects, 3 coverage, 4 threats, 5 STRIDE checklist), which the architect reads on the Security tab under Document Output. Asked what security gaps SDEM reports, quote review rather than working them out from the links. A record coverage marks unprotected is unprotected in this design: say so as a fact, without judging whether it should be. The Security tab's tiles also count what a control protects through what holds it; when giving a number, say which count it is.
writes: nothing in the workspace; security records only through sdem change propose (a person accepts)
licence: Apache-2.0; the NIST catalogue extract is public domain (catalogue.json, source)
contract: SDEM extension contract EXT-01…EXT-15 and metamodel extensions MX-01…MX-15 (taumoeps/bian-sdem-framework)

viewer.note: EL-01: what this extension offers a viewer. The DESNRE site decides which of it it shows (its extension registry, EL-02).

scope.note: vertical: a layer beside the design's layers whose links reach every one (LR-11). A horizontal extension would say {"within": ["A4"]}.

builds_on.note: MX-41, MX-11b: what this extension names in SDEM — an upgrade that renames or removes one of these must be checked against it first.

protected_means: a record is protected when a control that can act (not retired, deprecated or not_applicable) PROTECTS it; a field (A3.DataAttribute) also when its data entity is (MX-25). The DESNRE tiles also count what a control protects through what holds it, and say so.
